name: Somali
notes: Somali in the official Latin orthography (1972). C = pharyngeal /ʕ/; X = pharyngeal /ħ/; DH = retroflex /ɖ/, an intervocalic retroflex flap [ɽ] (Wikipedia, Somali language: "pronounced as a retroflex flap [ɽ] when it occurs intervocalically"; Mohamed 2013 hedges it to "sometimes pronounced as a flap", so the stop is kept as the second candidate). Q = uvular /q/; KH = uvular fricative /χ/, confined to Arabic loans (Mohamed 2013: "The sound /χ/ is a voiceless uvular fricative and is represented as <kh>"). Vowel length is phonemic and written by doubling the vowel letter. The apostrophe writes /ʔ/ (Mohamed 2013: "The sound /ʔ/ is a glottal stop, written as <’>"), and a WORD-INITIAL glottal stop is pronounced but never written: every orthographically vowel-initial word gets a prosthetic [ʔ] onset (Mohamed 2013, p.10: "the word initial glottal stop <'> - [ʔ] is also not shown"; and "When a Somali word begins with a vowel, a glottal is inserted before the vowel, in order to provide onset to the syllable ... <ey> 'dog' is transcribed and pronounced as [ʔey]"). That prosthesis is encoded in positional_graphemes rather than in the flat grapheme table so it fires only at the word edge. TWO THINGS THE ORTHOGRAPHY DOES NOT WRITE and this transcriber therefore cannot recover. (1) TONE: Somali is a pitch-accent language whose high/low accent carries gender, number and case, and the 1972 orthography leaves it unmarked; it is not derivable from spelling. (2) VOWEL HARMONY: the ten vowel qualities fall into two [±ATR] harmonic sets, and the orthography writes one letter per pair — as the Wikipedia article puts it, it "does not distinguish between the two harmonic variants of each vowel" — so the harmonic value of a root is lexical, not orthographic. The spec emits the plain five-quality set /a e i o u/ and their long counterparts. Narrow-transcription gold sets that write both tone and the ATR-distinct cardinal vowels (ɑ ɪ ɔ ɛ ʊ æ) score those unwritten distinctions as segment errors; that cost is notation, not a transcriber defect. AFFRICATE: ⟨j⟩ is the language's only affricate and is attested with both voicing values — Mohamed 2013 (consonant-inventory section): "The sound /ʧ/ or /ʤ/ is the only affricative, and it is the palato-alveolar affricative, orthographically represented as <j>. It can be pronounced like <ch> as in the English word <church>. It also can be pronounced like <j> as in the English word like <jingle>. Both pronunciations are correct." The voiced /dʒ/ stays the first candidate because that is the single value the consonant charts of Saeed 1999 and Gabbard 2010 carry (as tabulated in the Wikipedia Somali language article, whose consonant table cites Saeed 1999:7-10 and Gabbard 2010:6; neither chart consulted directly for this entry), with the voiceless /tʃ/ added as the second candidate on Mohamed's authority. The kaikki gold writes the voiceless value in 6 of 8 words (jeer, jir, jasiirad, jid, jilib, jidh take [tʃ]; cinjir and jecel take [dʒ]), so promoting it would lower PER; that is declined — a gold's preference among two attested variants is not evidence about which is primary. DIPHTHONGS: Somali has five short diphthongs written ⟨ay aw ey oy ow⟩ and five long ones written ⟨aay eey ooy aaw oow⟩ (Mohamed 2013, "Diphthongs": "Somali has five short and five long diphthongs"; ⟨aw⟩ "is pronounced like the English diphthong [au]", ⟨ey⟩ "like the English [ei]"). The second element is therefore a VOCALIC OFFGLIDE [i]/[u], not the consonant phonemes /j w/, so ⟨y⟩ and ⟨w⟩ take offglide values after ⟨a e o⟩ and keep their consonant values between vowels, where they are the onset of the next syllable (⟨hooyo⟩ [hoːjo], ⟨iyo⟩ [ʔijo]). Analyses that read the same sequences as coda /j w/ are also current, so the glide is kept as the second candidate. INTERVOCALIC LENITION: /b d ɡ/ have spirantized allophones [β ð ɣ] between vowels. /d/ and /ɡ/ rest on Armstrong 1964, reported in Bruhn, *Somali and the Nature of Morphophonological Alternations*: "Somali /g/ sometimes appears as [ɣ] between vowels" and "/d/ often lenites to [ð] between vowels" — both sources hedge the process as variable. /b/ rests on a separate primary source, Gabbard 2010, whose own fieldwork data show the alternation directly: the bare/plural pair [la:b] / [la:βo] "chest" shows [b] alternating with [β] across the plural suffix, and the underlying form /dɪbn/ "cheek, buttock" surfaces as [dɪβɪn] once an earlier-ordered copy-vowel rule breaks up the cluster and puts [b] between vowels (Gabbard 2010, p.17-18: the copy-vowel epenthesis rule is ordered before spirantization, so at the point spirantization applies the root is already dɪbɪn and the [b] is intervocalic). Gabbard treats the rule as regular rather than variable, but the stop is kept as the first candidate here for consistency with the hedged /d/ and /ɡ/ entries, and the fricative is offered as the second. GOLD FLOOR (kaikki/Wiktionary, n=230, crowd-scraped narrow transcription, measured via the board's own evaluate_words(strip_stress=True, broad=True) path): 21.3% of all gold characters (335/1570) are bare combining tone diacritics (acute, grave, macron, circumflex) that the 1972 orthography does not write, and a further 21.1% (332/1570) are the [±ATR] vowel letters ɑ ɪ ɛ ɔ æ ʉ the orthography collapses (ʊ is listed in some surveys of the inventory but does not occur in this gold set). Stripping tone and folding the ATR letters onto the five plain qualities takes the measured PER from 0.58 to 0.23 (0.2290) if only the bare combining marks are stripped, because a further minority of gold tone marks fuse with their vowel into a single precomposed codepoint (e.g. ú, ǽ) that a plain strip does not touch; decomposing those to NFD first before stripping is what the orthography's own unmarked-tone claim requires, and doing so brings the same two-fold operation to 0.17 (0.1711). Reaching a lower floor needs two further, narrower folds on top of the NFD-decomposed tone-and-ATR fold: collapsing the annotator's mid-central rounded ɞ onto o (0.1613), and separately stripping the devoicing rings the annotator places on some word-final obstruents (0.1553); with all four folds applied together the measured PER is 0.15 (0.1455). Two further notation folds, not previously accounted for, reach lower still: this gold writes vowel length as a DOUBLED LETTER (caano, aayo) where the engine writes the length mark ː, and collapsing both notations to a single vowel takes the four-fold number to 0.11 (0.1107); stripping the aspiration the annotator writes on voiceless stops (keen, kac) takes it to 0.10 (0.1029); folding the annotator's epiglottal letters ʡ ʢ ʜ onto the pharyngeals the spec emits takes it to 0.09 (0.0889). All six folds together leave 73.5% of words matching exactly. The residue is dominated by the glottal-stop-plus-devoiced-copy notation described below. Word-final devoicing in this gold set is mostly written a different way the folds above do not reach — an inserted glottal stop before a voiceless copy of the final obstruent (⟨laab⟩ as laaʔp, ⟨diid⟩ as diiʔt) — for which no source describing general Somali final devoicing was found, so it stays unencoded and unfolded; that residue, plus geminate ⟨r⟩ and the annotator's narrow epiglottal notation for /ʕ/ and /q/, accounts for most of what is left of the 0.15 floor. Stripping tone alone (no ATR fold), the same mechanism the harness already uses for Scandinavian pitch-accent digits, measures 0.46 (0.4641) without NFD and 0.41 (0.4092) with NFD. GOLD COMPOSITION: a fresh pull of the kaikki.org Somali dump (230 entries, same load_kaikki() filters as the board) breaks down by Wiktionary part of speech as 158 noun, 35 verb, 13 adj, 11 num, 6 pron, 3 prep, 2 suffix, 1 particle, 1 name — only 2/230 (0.9%) are bound morphemes, and the loader already excludes the ``character`` POS that would otherwise pull in alphabet-chart rows. This row is not padded with non-running-word entries the way some other rows in the same audit were; the gap is tone notation and the unwritten ATR harmony, not gold composition. WORD-INITIAL KH GUARD: a proposed word-initial bound-morpheme guard for positional rules (candidate: Somali ⟨kh⟩) does not apply to this spec — ⟨kh⟩ has no ``positional_graphemes`` entry at all, only the flat grapheme table value /χ/, so there is no word-initial rule to guard against a bound-morpheme false trigger. See ``tests/test_cited_rules_african_misc.py::test_so_kh_has_no_word_initial_positional_rule``.

sources.notes: Consulted directly. Own-fieldwork data documenting the intervocalic spirantization rule for /b d ɡ q/, e.g. the bare/plural pair [la:b] / [la:βo] 'chest' and the underlying form /dɪbn/ 'cheek, buttock', which surfaces as [dɪβɪn] once an earlier-ordered copy-vowel rule makes the /b/ intervocalic. The only source found that covers /b/ -> [β]; unlike Armstrong/Bruhn on /d/ and /ɡ/, Gabbard analyzes the rule as regular rather than variable.
